precepts.text: Whoso feareth the Lord shall direct his friendship aright: for as he is, so shall his neighbour be also. My son, gather instruction from thy youth up: so shalt thou find wisdom till thine old age. If you fear the Lord you are going to direct your friendships aright, because as you are, so shall your neighbour be also. But if you are constantly having issues, constantly having problems, who is the issue? Who is causing these troubles? Because with the laws of God you should be able to direct your friendship aright. So why is your name always in something? And gather instruction from thy youth up: we did not have that opportunity. But we have to be born again coming into this truth and begin to do so. You cannot drag in all the ways your grandmother and your auntie used to deal with each other. It is a new day.
precepts.point: I used to be a murderer. The law said thou shalt not murder. I used to be a thief. The law said thou shalt not steal. I used to be an abuser. Once I know the Lord, now I repent. Guess what, brother? Same thing. Guess what, sister? Same thing with your trauma. Stop using your trauma as a crutch. That happened when you were 14, 15, 16. You are still using that. Now you are 46, you are 50, and you are still using that. Some of you are in your third marriage and you still cannot keep a man, you cannot keep a woman, because of your trauma. You cannot cope.

note.label: Destructive Behaviors Among Our People

precepts.why:
“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul.” The law of God is perfect, it is pure, there is nothing wrong with it, and converting means to change. Only the law can change you. I used to be a murderer; the law said thou shalt not murder. I used to be a thief; the law said thou shalt not steal. I used to be an abuser. Once I know the Lord, I repent. Same thing, brother. Same thing, sister, with your trauma. Stop using your trauma as a crutch. It happened when you were 14, 15, 16, and now you're 46, 50, in your third marriage, still using it, and you can't keep a man or a woman because you cannot cope.

We never grew up around order, structure and unity. So when we come around it now, we begin to feel uncomfortable, because we realize we are the problem: the reason environments become toxic, the reason people bicker and fight, the instigating spirit we grew up seeing. Now, in a body and a truth where the light shines on that, you are forced to change, and brothers and sisters do not want to.

“Whoso feareth the Lord shall direct his friendship aright: for as he is, so shall his neighbour be also.” If you fear the Lord, you are going to direct your friendships aright, because as you are, so shall your neighbour be. But if you are constantly having issues, constantly having problems, who is the issue? Who is causing these troubles? With the laws of God and all the examples in the scriptures, you should be able to direct your friendship aright. So why is your name always in something?

“My son, gather instruction from thy youth up: so shalt thou find wisdom till thine old age.” We didn't have the opportunity to gather instruction from our youth up. But coming into this truth we have to be born again and begin to do so. You can't drag in all the ways your grandmama and your auntie and them used to deal with each other. It's a new day.

Destructive attitudes begin internally before they become visible externally. A person may still attend services, teach, lead, pray or serve while harboring the wrong spirit, an evil spirit. You look at the fringes and think, he's good, she's good; you would be surprised how many have an evil spirit in the midst of us. Some come here to destroy the unity of the brotherhood, because in the world it's always chaos: you never see a room full of black people with no fight, no argument, breaking bread together. Whatever you were going through in the world, you had better get over it, and quick, because that thing will destroy you. Those who carry that spirit will find themselves outside these doors.

precepts.text: The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul; the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple. The commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes: it will enlighten your spiritual eye to see clearly, to understand false speech, to know when you are going in the wrong direction. More to be desired are they than gold, sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb; but then it gets bitter, because now you start to learn about yourself. That is all right, because the law converts the soul. Moreover by them is thy servant warned: and in keeping of them there is great reward. Who can understand his errors? cleanse thou me from secret faults: things people do not know I am dealing with. Keep back thy servant also from presumptuous sins. This is a prayer we pray, and then God sends the prophets to tell you. So why are you upset? Do not ask for rain and get mad when it is muddy. Then shall I be upright, and innocent from the great transgression, and the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart shall be acceptable. If you want your words and thoughts to be acceptable, open this book, learn the will of God, and when the word comes to you, accept it for what it says. There is no speech nor language where their voice is not heard: whatever language you speak, the word will reach you; we will translate it. But you need to be cleansed.
precepts.point: For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty. That is the breath that was breathed into us in Genesis 2. If those are the attributes of wisdom, you want to be tethered to wisdom, so you can discern, so you understand why people do the things they do, so you know the intents of a person's heart when they speak.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
Wisdom is “a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty.” That is the breath that was breathed into us in Genesis 2; it was wisdom, so that we should know better. And what is pure? “The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes.” It will enlighten your spiritual eye to see things clearly, to understand false speech, to know when you're going in the wrong direction. It's supposed to light your path.

“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” “The fear of the Lord is clean, enduring for ever: the judgments of the Lord are true and righteous altogether. More to be desired are they than gold, yea, than much fine gold: sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb.” It is sweet, but then it gets bitter, because now you start to learn about yourself. That's all right, because the law of God converts the soul. It's only a problem when your soul isn't getting converted.

“Moreover by them is thy servant warned: and in keeping of them there is great reward.” The Lord does not ask us to keep the laws with nothing in return; he is a just and fair God. And converting doesn't just happen; you don't close your eyes and wake up different. It comes through trial, error and correction.

“Who can understand his errors? cleanse thou me from secret faults”: things people don't know I'm dealing with. Sometimes a class comes out talking right about you. You said you wanted wisdom. And if it comes in English and you speak Spanish, don't worry: “There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard.” We'll translate it, even into sign language. If it's for you, you'll get it. But you need to be cleansed.

“Keep back thy servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not have dominion over me.” This is a prayer we ask God for, and then he sends the prophets to tell you. So why are you upset? Don't ask for rain and get mad when it's muddy. You asked God to cleanse you; he has to show you what needs to be cleansed. The first key is listening. The greatest gift a young person can have is to listen: be neutral, hear what's being said, examine yourself whether it's true, and if it is, fix it. Stop lying to yourself.

“then shall I be upright, and I shall be innocent from the great transgression. Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be acceptable in thy sight, O Lord, my strength, and my redeemer.” If you want your words and your thoughts to be acceptable, open this book, learn what the will of God is, and when the word comes to you, accept it for what it says.

precepts.point: The bottle says you are alone, nobody understands us, I love you more than anybody. The bottle starts talking to you like it is scripture: drink me and I will take away thy sorrows, I am the comfort of them all. That is a spirit having a conversation with you.

note.label: The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

precepts.why:
The bottle says, you can't change. You're the same; you're going to be that same person. The Bible says, “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul.”

The law of the Lord converts the soul: it changes a man. So the lie that you can't change is answered by the perfect law of God. You can repent and become a new man.

That is the other side of casting your burden on the Lord. You don't just hand him the weight; you take on his law, and his law turns you into somebody different. The bottle keeps you drunk and stupid, the way the enemy wants it, with a liquor store in every black neighborhood and weed stores everywhere to keep you high, drunk and stupid. The law of the Lord makes the simple wise and converts the soul out of that.

precepts.text: There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard.
precepts.point: Others mocking said, These men are full of new wine. But Peter, standing up with the eleven, said, these are not drunken, as ye suppose, seeing it is but the third hour of the day. But this is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel: in the last days, saith God, I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy. Prophesy about what? The gathering of the twelve tribes of Israel; teaching the people who they are. The masses did not know; it was the job of the priests and the prophets to teach the people. But in the last days God is raising the message back up, and we are going out to raise our people back up and show them they are not Arabs and Muslims and African Americans or whatever label was put on them: we are the children of Israel.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
At Pentecost they “began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.” Other tongues means other languages. The psalm already said it: “There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard.”

There is no speech nor language where their voice is not heard. The devout men dwelling at Jerusalem came “out of every nation under heaven”, because according to Deuteronomy 28 we were going to be scattered into all nations. Every man heard the apostles speak in his own language, and they marvelled, “are not all these which speak Galileans?” That is because we were scattered among the heathen and learned their languages.

So God made sure the word reached every one of them in the tongue wherein they were born. In every language the scattered people of Israel had taken on, their voice was heard, and the gathering of the twelve tribes began.

precepts.text: The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the laws are what convert a man.
precepts.point: What converts us is the law of the Lord, which is perfect, converting the soul.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.why:
Peter says, “Repent ye therefore, and be converted”: converted means changed. But what converts us? David answers: “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul.” The laws of God are perfect, and they are what convert the soul. So back in Acts 3, when Peter says repent and be converted, what converts us is the laws of God.

That conversion is what makes the rest of the verse possible: “that your sins may be blotted out”, forgotten, washed away, “when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord.” The times of refreshing are the times of the kingdom being brought upon the earth, when the earth is refreshed.

Ezekiel shows what repentance means in the Old Testament, read right alongside it: “Therefore I will judge you, O house of Israel, every one according to his ways, saith the Lord God. Repent, and turn yourselves from all your transgressions.” When you repent, you turn away from your transgressions. You turn from sin, and the perfect law of the Lord is what turns you and changes your soul.

God is a God of those that repent, as Manasseh found. He did not call the righteous but sinners to repentance, and the way a sinner is converted is by coming under the law of the Lord.

precepts.text: The law converts the soul, the testimony makes wise the simple, the commandment is pure and enlightens the eyes. The pure influence of Wisdom of Solomon 7:25 is the statutes of God, and once converted we are new.
precepts.point: In all ages she enters holy souls and makes them friends of God and prophets. She cannot dwell in a body subject to sin, hypocrisy, covetousness, or hatred. When you move like that you start saying absurd things. A prophet's job is to raise up God's children, which is why he cannot walk in hypocrisy.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
Wisdom is “a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.” Influence means to mold you and direct you. If wisdom is flowing down from the Almighty and it is influencing you, you are connected, tethered, with God. Or something else can be influencing you, and that will not be wisdom; it will be covetousness, lust, whatever it might be. Psalms 19 shows what that pure influence is.

“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” We were once simple, but wisdom is now in us, making us wise. “The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes.”

That pure influence is the statutes, the laws of God. The commandment is “pure”, and it enlightens the eyes so that we can see clearly.

And if our eyes are enlightened and the Lord has converted us, what are we now? We are new, something different. That is where Wisdom of Solomon 7:27 goes: “remaining in herself, she maketh all things new.”

precepts.text: How shall they hear without a preacher, and how shall they preach except they be sent? Faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God. Have they not heard? Yes verily, their sound went into all the earth.
precepts.point: The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul; the testimony is sure, making wise the simple. People hunt for discrepancies over how many horses Solomon had, but the ten commandments are perfect and only the law converts the soul.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
David says “Day unto day uttereth speech, and night unto night sheweth knowledge”, and “Their line is gone out through all the earth”. You might think that speech and knowledge is the sun, the moon and the stars. No, it is the teachers, brothers out teaching day by day and night by night. Paul broke it down for us so we don't have to do guesswork: “But I say, Have they not heard? Yes verily, their sound went into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.” Paul is quoting Psalm 19, and their sound is the sound of teaching.

Start at verse 14: “How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher?” Our people cannot call on the Lord if they have not heard. You need a preacher to hear this gospel. “And how shall they preach, except they be sent?” To preach is to prophesy, and it takes being sent. “How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!” That is why brothers are told: be prepared. Prepare yourself to be sent.

“Lord, who hath believed our report?” The report is the Bible, the scriptures. The prophets preach the report, and the question is who has believed it.

“So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.” That is how you increase faith. New brothers and sisters ask how to increase their faith: you must consistently addict yourself to the hearing of the gospel, over and over. However old you are, calculate it: that is how many years of brainwashing you must undo. Coming in once a week will not undo it. It must be daily listening to the word, and reading more than the four chapters a day.

And whose sound is going into all the earth? All praises to the Lord for favouring this teaching. The doctrine of having sex with as many women as you can and not taking care of the babies is not going throughout all the earth. The groups talking about raping women and having concubines, the garbage teaching that John the Baptist is a wicked Israelite, the teaching that we are under the old covenant of animal sacrifice: none of that is going throughout the earth. The line that has gone out is repentance for the twelve tribes of Israel in the name of our king whom the world calls Jesus the Christ, heard now in all languages.

precepts.point: Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double minded.

note.label: Kill Or Be Killed

precepts.why:
James says God “giveth grace unto the humble”, and calls on them: “Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.” Paul says Christ cleanses his people “with the washing of water by the word.” David shows what that word is and what it does: “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.”

The law of the Lord is perfect, and that is what is going to cleanse you. That is what makes you perfect. Keeping the commandments is the cleansing. It converts the soul: it turns the old man into a new man, and makes the simple wise.

That is how you purify your mind. Remove from you the old ways, the old worldly mindset. You cannot get that cleansing from the white man's couch or from cashing a check; pay all the bills and you will still feel empty without the Lord in your life. Submit yourselves to his will, to his law, statutes and commandments, and resist the devil, the deceiver: his lies, the Trinity, the apologetics, the false doctrines of the other nations, and the world, point blank, period.

The more you apply the law and read, the more the Lord draws nigh to you and opens his understanding to you: the dark mysteries and the parables, how to guide your household, and how to stand in the temptations, trials and lusts that come your way. The perfect law is the weapon that kills the old man.

precepts.text: The testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple; it is the laws of the Most High that must be taught, for his laws change the people, not our testimony.
precepts.point: The testimony is the commandments of the Most High. If the children keep his covenant and his testimony, their children shall sit upon the throne for evermore; and it is his testimony, not our own testimony, that is righteous and very faithful and that changes the people.

note.label: Numbers 10: The Silver Trumpets and the Order of the Journeys

precepts.why:
“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” The testimony of the tabernacle of the testimony is the law of the Most High, and it is sure.

It is the laws of the Most High that must be taught, for His laws change the people, not our testimony. The law converts the soul and makes wise the simple. Our own testimony does not do that; His does.

That is what the children of Israel carried out of the wilderness of Sinai when the cloud was taken up: the testimony of the Lord, righteous, very faithful, and sure.

precepts.point: The line is gone out through all the earth, the gospel going out to the end of the world, and in them he set a tabernacle for the sun.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“Their line is gone out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world.” That is the gospel going out to the end of the world. And what is the gospel about? “For as a young man marrieth a virgin, so shall thy sons marry thee: and as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee.”

As a young man marries a virgin, so shall thy sons marry thee; as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee. The gospel is about us being joined back to Christ, the bridegroom rejoicing over his bride.

precepts.why:

The law is perfect, without lies. The law of the Lord being perfect means going into perfection with our lives: the law takes us there, and wisdom is perfection to a faithful mouth.

Why is the testimony so sure? “God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it? or hath he spoken, and shall he not make it good?”

God is not a man that he should lie. Whatever he has said, he will do it; whatever he has spoken, he will make it good. That is why the testimony of the Lord is sure: he will perform his word.

precepts.text: Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done; that is what prophecy is, and we have a sure word of it.
precepts.point: The testimony of the Lord is sure; the testimonies and prophecies in this Bible are sure.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure”. That is what prophecy is: the Most High declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things not yet done.

His counsel shall stand, and we have a sure word of it. That is the testimony of the Lord that is sure, making wise the simple.

precepts.text: Smite a scorner and the simple will beware; the scorner is called simple, and these words are synonymous.
precepts.point: Making wise the simple: pay attention to who the simple is, the scorner, the foolish, the youth void of understanding. A lot of times we go out and think the scorner is somebody who does not want to hear, but it also goes into a youth who thinks he knows something but really does not.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” Pay attention to who the simple is. “Smite a scorner, and the simple will beware: and reprove one that hath understanding, and he will understand knowledge.”

Smite a scorner and the simple will beware: the scorner is called simple. These words are synonymous. A lot of times we think the scorner is somebody who does not want to hear, but the simple one is the same person.

precepts.text: When the scorner is punished the simple is made wise; that is making wise the simple.
precepts.point: Making wise the simple: pay attention to who the simple is, the scorner, the foolish, the youth void of understanding. A lot of times we go out and think the scorner is somebody who does not want to hear, but it also goes into a youth who thinks he knows something but really does not.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“When the scorner is punished, the simple is made wise: and when the wise is instructed, he receiveth knowledge.” When the scorner is punished, the simple is made wise. That is “making wise the simple” in Psalm 19:7.

Again the scorner and the simple are the same one. The testimony of the Lord is sure, and it makes the simple wise.

precepts.text: How long ye simple ones will ye love simplicity, and the scorners delight in their scorning, and fools hate knowledge; simple, scorner and fool are synonyms.
precepts.point: Making wise the simple: pay attention to who the simple is, the scorner, the foolish, the youth void of understanding. A lot of times we go out and think the scorner is somebody who does not want to hear, but it also goes into a youth who thinks he knows something but really does not.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“How long, ye simple ones, will ye love simplicity? and the scorners delight in their scorning, and fools hate knowledge?” Simple ones loving simplicity, scorners delighting in their scorning, fools hating knowledge: simple, scorner and fool are synonyms.

So the simple that the sure testimony of the Lord makes wise is the scorner and the fool, the one who has been loving simplicity and hating knowledge.

precepts.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and instruction.
precepts.point: Making wise the simple: pay attention to who the simple is, the scorner, the foolish, the youth void of understanding. A lot of times we go out and think the scorner is somebody who does not want to hear, but it also goes into a youth who thinks he knows something but really does not.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.” Knowledge begins with the fear of the Lord, and the fool is the one who despises wisdom and instruction.

That fool is the simple and the scorner of Proverbs 1:22, the one the testimony of the Lord makes wise once he stops despising instruction.

precepts.text: He looked through his casement and beheld among the simple ones a young man void of understanding; simple means you are void of understanding, the youth.
precepts.point: Making wise the simple: pay attention to who the simple is, the scorner, the foolish, the youth void of understanding. A lot of times we go out and think the scorner is somebody who does not want to hear, but it also goes into a youth who thinks he knows something but really does not.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“For at the window of my house I looked through my casement, And beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the youths, a young man void of understanding”. Solomon looked through his casement and saw among the simple ones a young man void of understanding.

Simple means you are void of understanding, the youth. The simple is not only somebody who does not want to hear; it also goes into a youth who thinks he knows something but really does not. That is who the testimony of the Lord makes wise.

precepts.text: An instructor of the foolish, a teacher of babes; there go the synonyms, foolish and babes and youth, so we must come back as a baby knowing we do not know anything.
precepts.point: Making wise the simple: pay attention to who the simple is, the scorner, the foolish, the youth void of understanding. A lot of times we go out and think the scorner is somebody who does not want to hear, but it also goes into a youth who thinks he knows something but really does not.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“An instructor of the foolish, a teacher of babes, which hast the form of knowledge and of the truth in the law.” There go the synonyms again: foolish and babes, like the simple and the youth void of understanding.

The form of knowledge and of the truth is in the law, and it is taught to the foolish and to babes. So we must come back as a baby, knowing we do not know anything, and let the sure testimony of the Lord make the simple wise.

precepts.text: The light of the body is the eye; if thine eye be single thy whole body is full of light, but if thine eye be evil thy body is full of darkness; keep the commandment as the apple of your eye.
precepts.point: The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart; the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes. When the commandments enlighten your eyes you know where to walk, you will not stumble, you stay focused on keeping God's laws.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes.” Christ says, “The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light. But if thine eye be evil, thy whole body shall be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is that darkness!”

If your eye is single, your whole body is full of light; if it is evil, your body is full of darkness. Keep the commandment as the apple of your eye. When the commandments enlighten your eyes, you know where to walk, you will not stumble, and you stay focused on keeping God's laws.

precepts.text: Keep my commandments and live, and my law as the apple of thine eye.
precepts.point: The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart; the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes. When the commandments enlighten your eyes you know where to walk, you will not stumble, you stay focused on keeping God's laws.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.” Keep the commandments and live, and keep the law as the apple of your eye.

That is the commandment of the Lord enlightening the eyes. With the law as the apple of your eye, your eye is single and your whole body is full of light, and you know where to walk.

precepts.text: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet and a light unto my path; the word enlightens your eyes and becomes a light to navigate life.
precepts.point: The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart; the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes. When the commandments enlighten your eyes you know where to walk, you will not stumble, you stay focused on keeping God's laws.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.” The word enlightens your eyes and becomes a light to navigate life.

With the commandment of the Lord enlightening the eyes, you can see the path, you will not stumble, and you stay focused on keeping God's laws. The word is the lamp to the feet and the light to the path.

precepts.text: He is a rock, his work is perfect, for all his ways are judgment, a God of truth and without iniquity; all the ways of the Lord are judgment.
precepts.point: The fear of the Lord is clean, enduring for ever; the judgments of the Lord are true and righteous altogether. This whole Bible is the ways of the Lord, the judgments of the Lord, true and righteous altogether; if you want to know what righteousness is you have to learn and follow the Bible.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“the judgments of the Lord are true and righteous altogether.” Moses says: “He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he.”

He is a rock, his work is perfect, and all his ways are judgment, a God of truth and without iniquity. This whole Bible is the ways of the Lord, the judgments of the Lord, true and righteous altogether. If you want to know what righteousness is, you have to learn and follow the Bible.

precepts.text: Days should speak and multitude of years should teach wisdom, but great men are not always wise, neither do the aged understand judgment; the multitude of years should have taught our people wisdom about the judgments, but they do not have it.
precepts.point: The fear of the Lord is clean, enduring for ever; the judgments of the Lord are true and righteous altogether. This whole Bible is the ways of the Lord, the judgments of the Lord, true and righteous altogether; if you want to know what righteousness is you have to learn and follow the Bible.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“I said, Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom.” The multitude of years should have taught our people wisdom about the judgments of the Lord, but they do not have it.

“But there is a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding. Great men are not always wise: neither do the aged understand judgment.” Understanding comes from the inspiration of the Almighty, not from age; great men are not always wise, and the aged do not understand judgment.

The judgments of the Lord are true and righteous altogether, and to know them you have to learn and follow the Bible, not lean on years.

precepts.text: By these, my son, be admonished; of making many books there is no end; you do not need to search out a lot of books thinking wisdom is missing, these books right here are what you need.
precepts.point: More to be desired are they than gold, yea than much fine gold, sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb; moreover by them is thy servant warned.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
The judgments of the Lord are “More to be desired are they than gold, yea, than much fine gold”. Solomon says: “And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.”

By these be admonished. You do not need to search out a lot of books thinking wisdom is missing; of making many books there is no end. These books right here are what you need, more to be desired than fine gold and sweeter than honey.

precepts.text: Seek ye out of the book of the Lord and read; no one of these shall fail, none shall want her mate, for his mouth it hath commanded; this Bible is a collection of our records.
precepts.point: More to be desired are they than gold, yea than much fine gold, sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb; moreover by them is thy servant warned.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read: no one of these shall fail, none shall want her mate: for my mouth it hath commanded, and his spirit it hath gathered them.” Seek out of the book of the Lord and read; none of these shall fail, none shall want her mate, for his mouth commanded it.

This Bible is a collection of our records. That is why it is more to be desired than much fine gold, sweeter than honey and the honeycomb: it is the book of the Lord, gathered by his spirit.

precepts.text: Search me O God and know my heart, try me and know my thoughts, and see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting; God knows your thoughts, so let him try you.
precepts.point: Who can understand his errors? Cleanse thou me from secret faults. This should be your reason to be in this walk, not to appear righteous, but because God shall bring every work into judgment; work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“Who can understand his errors? cleanse thou me from secret faults.” David prays the same way here: “Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts: And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.”

God knows your thoughts, so let him try you. Ask him to search your heart, to see if there is any wicked way in you, and to lead you in the way everlasting. That is asking to be cleansed from secret faults, the ones you cannot understand yourself.

precepts.text: Work out your own salvation with fear and trembling, now much more in his absence; this goes into cleansing you from secret faults.
precepts.point: Who can understand his errors? Cleanse thou me from secret faults. This should be your reason to be in this walk, not to appear righteous, but because God shall bring every work into judgment; work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“Wherefore, my beloved, as ye have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.” Work out your own salvation with fear and trembling, now much more in his absence, when nobody is watching.

This goes into cleansing you from secret faults. Your reason to be in this walk should not be to appear righteous, but because God shall bring every work into judgment.

precepts.text: Stand in awe and sin not, commune with your own heart upon your bed and be still; know yourself in your alone time and ask what you can do.
precepts.point: Who can understand his errors? Cleanse thou me from secret faults. This should be your reason to be in this walk, not to appear righteous, but because God shall bring every work into judgment; work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“Stand in awe, and sin not: commune with your own heart upon your bed, and be still. Selah.” Stand in awe and sin not; commune with your own heart upon your bed and be still.

Know yourself in your alone time and ask what you can do. That is how you get at the secret faults: not to appear righteous before others, but to be cleansed where only God sees.

precepts.text: The house of Stephanas addicted themselves to the ministry of the saints; studying in your alone time should become an addiction, a righteous addiction that replaces idleness.
precepts.point: Who can understand his errors? Cleanse thou me from secret faults. This should be your reason to be in this walk, not to appear righteous, but because God shall bring every work into judgment; work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
Paul commends the house of Stephanas, “that it is the firstfruits of Achaia, and that they have addicted themselves to the ministry of the saints”. They addicted themselves to the ministry.

Studying in your alone time should become an addiction like that, a righteous addiction that replaces idleness. That is how you work at being cleansed from secret faults.

precepts.text: A cry to have discipline set over your thoughts, lest ignorance increase to destruction and you commit that great transgression.
precepts.point: Keep back thy servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not have dominion over me; then shall I be upright and innocent from the great transgression. A sin addiction has to be replaced with a righteous addiction, because change does not just up and happen when you are accustomed to doing evil.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“Keep back thy servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not have dominion over me”. Here is the same cry: “O Lord, Father and Governor of all my whole life, leave me not to their counsels, and let me not fall by them. Who will set scourges over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom over mine heart? that they spare me not for mine ignorances, and it pass not by my sins”.

It is a cry to have discipline set over your thoughts, “Lest mine ignorances increase, and my sins abound to my destruction, and I fall before mine adversaries, and mine enemy rejoice over me”. Ignorance left alone increases to destruction, and that is how you commit the great transgression.

“Turn away from me vain hopes and concupiscence, and thou shalt hold him up that is desirous always to serve thee. Let not the greediness of the belly nor lust of the flesh take hold of me; and give not over me thy servant into an impudent mind.” A sin addiction has to be replaced with a righteous addiction, because change does not just up and happen when you are accustomed to doing evil. Ask for the scourges over your thoughts, and sins will not have dominion over you.

precepts.text: The law of the Most High is perfect, converting the soul; the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.
precepts.point: If each of us took a strong look at ourselves, we are more wise than before we came into the knowledge of the truth, because we should be growing in understanding as we continue to apply the commandments. The scriptures are spiritual; the law is spiritual.

note.label: Psalm 93: The Lord Reigneth and His Testimonies Are Sure

precepts.why:
“Thy testimonies are very sure: holiness becometh thine house, O Lord, for ever.” David says the same in Psalm 19: “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.”

The law of the Most High is perfect, converting the soul, and his testimony is sure, making wise the simple. If each of us took a strong look at ourselves, we are more wise than before we came into the knowledge of the truth, because we should be growing in understanding as we continue to apply the commandments.

The scriptures are spiritual; the law is spiritual. That is how a sure testimony makes the simple wise and converts the soul, and how holiness comes to fit his house.

precepts.text: The heavens declare the glory of God; their line is gone out through all the earth, and that line is the gospel, the laws of God going out through the brothers teaching to the four corners of the earth.
precepts.point: The heavens declare His righteousness and all the people see His glory. How do all the people see His glory? Israel, the so-called blacks, Hispanics, and native Indians, are His glory.

note.label: Psalm 97: A Fire Goeth Before Him

precepts.why:
“The heavens declare his righteousness, and all the people see his glory.” David says the same at the start of Psalm 19: “The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork. Day unto day uttereth speech, and night unto night sheweth knowledge.”

“There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard. Their line is gone out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world.” That line is the gospel, the laws of God, going out through the brothers teaching to the four corners of the earth.

And how do all the people see his glory? Israel, the so-called blacks, Hispanics and native Indians, are his glory. As the line goes out, you see Israel coming back to their nationality and seeing his glory: the men are pure gold, the leaders of the earth, the kings and priests of the earth.

precepts.text: The law of the Most High is perfect, converting the soul; it is the law that converts us so that our eyes can be opened.
precepts.point: I am a stranger in the earth; hide not Thy commandments from me. Thou hast rebuked the proud that are cursed, which do err from Thy commandments. His testimonies are the delight of the servant and his counselors even when princes sit and speak against him.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” It is the law that converts us, so that our eyes can be opened to behold wondrous things out of it.

That is why the prayer is to keep his word and have his eyes opened together: the law converts the soul, and the converted eyes see. His testimonies become the servant's delight and his counsellors, even when princes sit and speak against him.

precepts.text: A prayer for the last days, that the Lord cleanse us from secret faults and keep us back from presumptuous sins, that they not have dominion over us, so we be upright and innocent from the great transgression.
precepts.point: Who is wise, and he shall understand these things? Prudent, and he shall know them? For the ways of the Lord are right, and the just shall walk in them, but the transgressors shall fall therein.

note.label: Hosea 14: O Israel, Return Unto the Lord

precepts.why:
Hosea asks “Who is wise, and he shall understand these things? prudent, and he shall know them?” The just walk in the ways of the Lord, but the transgressors fall therein. David’s words are a prayer for the last days: “Who can understand his errors? cleanse thou me from secret faults. Keep back thy servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not have dominion over me: then shall I be upright, and I shall be innocent from the great transgression.”

That is the prayer for us: that the Lord cleanse us from secret faults and keep us back from presumptuous sins, that they not have dominion over us, so we be upright and innocent from the great transgression, walking in his ways rather than falling in them.

precepts.text: The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul.
precepts.point: Peter walked with him and was not yet converted. What converts a man is named in the psalm, and what he strengthens his brethren with is the same thing.

note.label: Luke 22: The Passover, the Betrayal, and the Denial

precepts.why:
Christ tells Simon that Satan desired to sift him as wheat, “But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.” Peter had walked with him all that time and was not yet converted.

The psalm names what converts a man: “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” The law of the Lord converts the soul. So when Peter is converted, what he strengthens his brethren with is that same law.

precepts.text: Day unto day uttereth speech, and there is no speech nor language where their voice is not heard; their line is gone out through all the earth to the end of the world.
precepts.point: Because Israel was scattered among nations whose tongue they did not understand, the Most High spoke to his people with stammering lips and another tongue. The cloven tongues were the many languages of the lands where Israel was dispersed, and they spoke the word of the Most High in them like fire.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
David uses the same words the way Genesis 11 does: “Day unto day uttereth speech, and night unto night sheweth knowledge. There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard.” Speech and language are the same thing as tongues, and speech carries knowledge. A tongue is something that can be heard and understood, not babble.

“Their line is gone out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world.” The words go out to the end of the world in every speech and language. That is what the cloven tongues were: the word of the Most High going out in the many languages of the lands where Israel was dispersed.

precepts.text: The law of the Most High is perfect, converting the soul, so it is the law that converts and changes you, because sin infects down to the soul and becomes your character.
precepts.point: "Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord." People say they repented without understanding the scriptural meaning of the words. To repent is to turn from all your transgressions, and to be converted is to change, which requires the law to change to.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
To be converted is to change, and something has to change you: “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.”

It is the law that converts. Sin infects down to the soul and becomes your character, so conversion requires the law to change to. Repent, turn from your transgressions, and be converted by the law of the Most High, that your sins may be blotted out.

You want to stop being stupid, apply God's laws to your life. So if any one of you falls into those categories, just fix it.

note.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple. So the law of God is perfect. It is pure. There is nothing wrong with the law. Converting the soul: to change. Only the law can change you.

I used to be a murderer. The law said thou shalt not murder. I used to be a thief. The law said thou shalt not steal. I used to be an abuser. Once I know the Lord, now I repent. Guess what, brother? Same thing. Guess what, sister? Same thing with your trauma. Stop using your trauma as a crutch. That happened when you were 14, 15, 16. You are still using that. Now you are 46, you are 50, and you are still using that. Some of you are in your third marriage and you still cannot keep a man, you cannot keep a woman, because of your trauma. You cannot cope.

points: The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.

And with all this, if you know God is real, how much more should you realize him in your conversation and your actions of not sinning?

We are fulfilling those things we read in the scriptures right now.

points: Their line is gone out through all the earth: our line, our lineage, our legacy, your teaching, the works that you put in for this gospel's sake.

points: In them hath he set a tabernacle for the sun, which is as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber, and rejoiceth as a strong man to run a race. That is when the Lord says, well done, my good and faithful servant: you are a vessel made for honor, because you fulfilled the purpose he created you for.

Converting us from darkness into light, from the power of Satan unto the power of God, for the salvation and redemption of our souls. points: Let them not have dominion over me: if you do not, that thing will have dominion over you like the spirit had dominion over Cain, and he slew his brother. Then shall I be upright, and I shall be innocent from the great transgression.

points: Day unto day uttereth speech and night unto night sheweth knowledge: not the sun and stars but the teachers, teaching day and night. There is no speech nor language where their voice is not heard; their line is gone out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world. Romans 10:18 proves Paul read it as the sound of the gospel going into all the earth.

The line going out through all the earth is repentance for the twelve tribes in the name of Christ, not the doctrines of concubines, or John the Baptist as a wicked Israelite, or animal sacrifice under the old covenant. God has favoured this teaching.

points: In them hath he set a tabernacle for the sun: sanctuaries for the wisdom of the word in every state and country, fulfilling prophecy. The teacher is as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber and a strong man running a race; if you are boring, sit down.
